legend.title: Visual legend
legend.direction.outgoing_description: Outgoing edges to child or dependent tables visible in the diagram.

legend.table_type.entity_description: General business table that does not match the association or hierarchy heuristics.
legend.table_type.association_descriptio: Bridge table detected by several FKs and, when applicable, a composite PK made of relational columns.
legend.table_type.hierarchy_description: Self-referencing table that represents parent-child relationships within the same entity.
legend.relation_type.fk_description: Relationship type currently supported by the diagram renderer: foreign key.
legend.note.cardinality: Cardinality markers are shown apart from the edge to improve readability.
legend.note.colors: Table colors represent a heuristic visual typology of the node, not an absolute taxonomy of the data model.
legend.note.relation_types: The relationship type legend may grow when analysis exposes more real types besides FK.

diagram.help.outgoing: Outgoing relationships to child or dependent tables of the current table.
diagram.help.incoming: Incoming relationships from parent or referencing tables to the current table.
diagram.help.isolated: The table has no incoming or outgoing foreign keys: it is drawn alone.
diagram.hidden.outgoing: Hidden outgoing: levels of child or dependent tables that exist in the graph but are not shown because of the visible depth limit.
diagram.hidden.outgoing_count: Hidden outgoing: {count} level(s) of child or dependent tables that exist in the graph but are not shown because of the visible depth limit.
diagram.hidden.incoming: Hidden incoming: levels of parent or referencing tables that exist in the graph but are not shown because of the visible depth limit.
diagram.hidden.incoming_count: Hidden incoming: {count} level(s) of parent or referencing tables that exist in the graph but are not shown because of the visible depth limit.
diagram.tip.separate_directions: Review outgoing and incoming separately to avoid mixing child dependencies with referencing tables.
diagram.tip.hidden_levels: Some levels are not visible because of the depth limit: use the summary to decide whether you need to widen the scope of the diagram.
diagram.tip.incremental: When several levels are visible, start with Level 1 and move forward incrementally to keep context.
diagram.summary.title: Level summary
diagram.summary.line: Levels per direction: {depth} | Outgoing (tables it points to): {visible_outgoing} of {total_outgoing} | Incoming (tables pointing to it): {visible_incoming} of {total_incoming}
